# Computing $\int_T G^* \eta_{S^2}$

## Setup

The torus $T$ is generated by rotating the circle $\{(x,0,z) \mid (x-2)^2+z^2=1\}$ about the $z$-axis. This is a standard torus with major radius $R=2$ and minor radius $r=1$.

A parametrization is:
$$\mathbf{X}(\theta,\phi)=\big((2+\cos\phi)\cos\theta,\,(2+\cos\phi)\sin\theta,\,\sin\phi\big),\quad \theta,\phi\in[0,2\pi].$$

## The Gauss map

The outward unit normal at $\mathbf{X}(\theta,\phi)$ is
$$G(\theta,\phi)=\mathbf{n}(\theta,\phi)=(\cos\phi\cos\theta,\,\cos\phi\sin\theta,\,\sin\phi).$$

One verifies: $\mathbf{X}_\theta = (-(2+\cos\phi)\sin\theta,\,(2+\cos\phi)\cos\theta,\,0)$ and $\mathbf{X}_\phi=(-\sin\phi\cos\theta,\,-\sin\phi\sin\theta,\,\cos\phi)$, and $\mathbf{X}_\theta\times\mathbf{X}_\phi = (2+\cos\phi)\,\mathbf{n}$, confirming $\mathbf{n}$ is the outward unit normal.

## Pulling back the area form

Use spherical coordinates $(\alpha,\beta)$ on $S^2$ ($\alpha$ = polar angle from $+z$-axis, $\beta$ = azimuthal angle), so
$$\eta_{S^2}=\sin\alpha\,d\alpha\wedge d\beta.$$

Under $G$: the image point has $z$-coordinate $\sin\phi=\cos\alpha$, so $\alpha=\tfrac{\pi}{2}-\phi$, and azimuthal angle $\beta=\theta$. Hence
$$d\alpha=-d\phi,\qquad d\beta=d\theta,\qquad \sin\alpha=\sin(\tfrac{\pi}{2}-\phi)=\cos\phi.$$

Therefore
$$G^*\eta_{S^2}=\cos\phi\cdot(-d\phi)\wedge d\theta=\cos\phi\,d\theta\wedge d\phi.$$

## Evaluating the integral

$$\int_T G^*\eta_{S^2}=\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\int_0^{2\pi}\cos\phi\,d\theta\,d\phi=2\pi\int_0^{2\pi}\cos\phi\,d\phi=2\pi\cdot 0=0.$$

## Consistency check via Gauss–Bonnet

The pullback satisfies $G^*\eta_{S^2}=K\,dA$, where $K=\dfrac{\cos\phi}{(2+\cos\phi)}$ is the Gaussian curvature and $dA=(2+\cos\phi)\,d\theta\,d\phi$ is the area element, so $K\,dA=\cos\phi\,d\theta\,d\phi$, matching the direct computation. By Gauss–Bonnet,
$$\int_T K\,dA = 2\pi\,\chi(T)=2\pi\cdot 0=0,$$
since the torus has Euler characteristic $0$. Both methods agree.

## Result

$$\boxed{\int_T G^*\eta_{S^2}=0}$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
